articles.title: Kolter, BH Inch Toward Buyout on Oceanfront Miami Beach Condo
articles.narrative: Kolter Group and BH Group are nearing completion of an oceanfront site assemblage in Miami Beach, acquiring the majority of units within the Port Royale condo building for $61.6 million. This acquisition, combined with previous purchases of two neighboring hotels, will pave the way for a new luxury condominium development. The site, spanning approximately 2 acres, is slated for a 17-story, 37-unit condo project with ground-floor retail, designed by Kobi Karp.

data_points.notable_features: Oceanfront site assemblage between 69th and 71st streets, including two neighboring hotels; the Port Royale building was evacuated five years ago after being deemed unsafe.
data_points.project_notes: The developers previously acquired the 34,980-square-foot Normandy Plaza Hotel at 6985 Collins Avenue for $18 million in 2023, and the Crystal Beach Suites at 6979 Collins Avenue for $26 million in January 2026, along with its 7,600-square-foot commercial condos for $14.4 million in July 2026. Wells Fargo increased a loan tied to these properties to $83.2 million in September 2026. Plans were filed in September 2026 to demolish the Normandy Plaza Hotel, and in 2025 for a 37-unit condo development.

articles.title: Google Relocation Leads D.C.’s Office Market in Q3
articles.narrative: Washington, D.C.'s office market saw a steady third quarter with 1.8 million square feet leased, aligning with the five-year quarterly average. However, a significant disparity persists between trophy properties, which maintain below 10% availability, and the broader market. This scarcity in premier space is driving tenants, particularly law firms and government entities, to secure leases well in advance of expirations, prompting landlords to undertake building repositioning projects. The quarter's largest lease was a 210,000-square-foot consolidation by a major tech company.

articles.title: Bank of America, JLL Provide $276M Refi for SoCal Senior Housing
articles.narrative: An affiliate of Nexus Development secured $276 million in refinancing for two senior housing communities in Newport Beach, CA. Bank of America provided a $140 million loan for Vivante Newport Center, while JLL Real Estate Capital provided $136 million for Vivante Newport Mesa. The financing for Vivante Newport Center, at approximately $1.4 million per unit, represents one of the largest per-unit financings in the senior housing sector's history.

data_points.project_notes: The $140 million loan for Vivante Newport Center works out to roughly $1.4 million per unit, one of the largest financings on a per-unit basis in the senior housing industry's history.

articles.title: Sony in Talks to Anchor Tishman Speyer’s 99 Hudson Boulevard
articles.narrative: Sony is reportedly in negotiations to become the anchor tenant at Tishman Speyer's proposed 99 Hudson Boulevard in Hudson Yards, New York City. The electronics giant is seeking a larger, more collaborative workspace than its current 568,000-square-foot headquarters at 11 Madison Avenue. The planned 48-story, 1.256 million-square-foot office tower, designed by Henning Larsen, is expected to be an all-electric LEED Gold building, with construction slated to begin in December and occupancy by 2030. Tishman Speyer is seeking $92 million in property and mortgage tax exemptions from the city's Industrial Development Agency to support the project.

data_points.address: 99 Hudson Boulevard, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: All-electric LEED Gold tower with unobstructed views of the Hudson River, located opposite the Javits Center and facing Bella Abzug Park.
data_points.project_notes: Tishman Speyer is seeking $92 million in property tax exemptions and mortgage tax recording exemptions from the city's Industrial Development Agency, with a vote scheduled for November 17. The project is expected to generate nearly $274 million in direct and indirect taxes and create approximately 5,900 jobs.

articles.financing: The project is supported by a $1.477 billion loan and $1.2 billion in equity.

articles.title: Hines Promotes Adam Hines to Co-CEO Alongside Laura Hines-Pierce
Partnership Acquires 322-Unit Apartment Community in Denton, Texas
articles.narrative: A partnership between Spirit Investment Partners and Strategic Value Partners has acquired Resia Rayzor Ranch, a 322-unit apartment community in Denton, Texas. The property, built in 2024, was part of a two-property portfolio deal that also included a 573-unit community in Houston. JLL arranged acquisition financing for the transaction through Oaktree Capital Management.

data_points.notable_features: Amenities include a pool, fitness center, pickleball and basketball courts, outdoor grilling and dining stations, coworking space and package lockers.

articles.title: Newmark closes 157,642-square-foot office lease in Southfield
articles.narrative: Newmark recently facilitated a significant 157,642-square-foot office lease at Travelers Tower II in Southfield, Michigan. The transaction involved Time Equities, Inc. as the landlord and a tenant represented by JLL. This lease underscores the continued appeal of Class-A office space in the Southfield market, particularly in well-located and amenity-rich properties that have undergone substantial capital improvements.

data_points.notable_features: Class-A office building with renovated lobbies, fitness center, café, restrooms, elevator modernization, HVAC upgrades, conference center, tenant lounge, and outdoor patios. Located with convenient access to major regional thoroughfares.
data_points.project_notes: Travelers Towers complex comprises two interconnected office buildings totaling 810,460 square feet on a 21-acre site. Approximately 33,786 square feet remains available at Travelers Tower II following this lease.

articles.title: Draper and Kramer brokers $27.5 million in loans for industrial complex and multifamily property in Chicago area
articles.narrative: Draper and Kramer's Commercial Finance Group recently brokered two loans totaling $27.5 million for properties in the Chicago area. One loan, for $13.5 million, financed the acquisition of a three-building industrial complex in Bridgeview. The second transaction was a $14 million bridge loan for a newly constructed 56-unit multifamily property in Chicago's Edgewater neighborhood.

articles.title: Beyond the Headlines, CRE Is Thousands of Local Stories
articles.narrative: This article argues that the commercial real estate market is primarily driven by thousands of smaller, local transactions rather than the high-profile, institutional-scale deals that dominate headlines. The author, citing data from CoStar, Altus Group, and the Census Bureau, highlights that the majority of multifamily properties have fewer than 50 units, most retail leases are under 5,000 square feet, and the average commercial transaction is typically under $5 million. This disconnect between media coverage and market reality means that national data often fails to capture the nuances of local markets, where granular intelligence about specific properties, landlords, and zoning changes is crucial for successful deals. The article emphasizes that a distributed network, like REMAX Commercial, is better positioned to identify and execute these smaller, community-sustaining transactions.

articles.title: Capstone Equities Signs UK AI Tenant to First U.S. Location
articles.narrative: Conduct AI, a UK-based artificial intelligence company, has signed a lease for its first U.S. office at 140 Crosby St. in Manhattan's SoHo neighborhood. The company will occupy the entire 6,705-square-foot third floor of the boutique Class A office building. This transaction marks the first new lease at the property since Capstone Equities acquired ownership, demonstrating the building's appeal to fast-growing technology firms.

data_points.address: 140 Crosby St., New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Boutique Class A office building in SoHo.
data_points.project_notes: The landlord plans new investments in the property, including a renovation of its communal rooftop deck.

articles.title: North Hollywood Apartments Trade to Locally Based LLC
articles.narrative: A 41-unit multifamily property in North Hollywood, which had been under the same ownership for over 30 years, has been sold for nearly $5.89 million. The transaction closed at a 5.7% cap rate based on in-place income. The buyer, a San Fernando Valley-based LLC, plans to undertake common area and interior upgrades to reposition the asset.

data_points.project_notes: Property had been under the same ownership for over 30 years.

articles.title: Mojo Coffee Officially Opens in Chicago’s Loop
articles.narrative: Mojo Coffee has officially opened a new 1,576-square-foot cafe at 70 W. Madison in Chicago's Loop, occupying a ground-floor corner of the office tower. The New Zealand-born specialty roaster's opening follows significant leasing activity and ongoing investments in building upgrades by owners Namdar Realty Group and Mason Asset Management, who acquired the property in December 2024.

data_points.notable_features: Ground-floor corner retail space with street and direct lobby access.
data_points.project_notes: The building was acquired in December 2024 for $85 million. The space was previously occupied by a Starbucks.

articles.title: Charney Companies, Tavros Break Ground on Fifth Gowanus Development
articles.narrative: Charney Companies and Tavros have broken ground on 175 Third St., a 27-story mixed-use tower in Gowanus, Brooklyn. This project, which will feature over 1,000 apartments including approximately 250 affordable units, is the fifth development in the neighborhood by the co-developers and is part of the larger Gowanus Wharf development. The design incorporates a significant public waterfront esplanade, enhancing community access to the canal.

data_points.project_notes: Approximately 250 units will be affordable. This is the fifth development in Gowanus by the co-developers.

articles.title: Carnegie Mellon's Ken Griffin-Backed Campus Has Miami Developers Salivating
articles.narrative: Carnegie Mellon University's new campus in Miami, backed by a $3 billion investment from Ken Griffin, is generating significant interest among local developers. This substantial educational and financial commitment is expected to spur new development opportunities in the surrounding area, as developers look to capitalize on the anticipated growth and demand generated by the campus.

articles.title: Stockdale Found A Gap In The Debt Market. Then It Seized An Opportunity
articles.narrative: Stockdale, a Los Angeles-based firm, has launched a new credit strategy to capitalize on a perceived gap in the debt market. The strategy will focus on originating loans ranging from $15 million to $75 million, specifically targeting distressed assets and asset classes. This move allows Stockdale to provide financing solutions in a segment where traditional lenders may be more hesitant.

articles.title: Inside CareTrust's £1.1B UK Deal: How U.S. Investors Conquered Care Homes
articles.narrative: CareTrust, a U.S.-based investor, has acquired a portfolio of UK care homes for £1.1 billion. This transaction represents a significant cross-border investment, marking another instance of U.S. capital flowing into the UK's care home sector.

data_points.project_notes: Sale price is in British Pounds (£).

articles.title: University City Office Market Improves Despite Slow Quarter In Philly
articles.narrative: The University City and Navy Yard submarkets in Philadelphia demonstrated resilience in the third quarter, securing the city's largest office leases despite a broader trend of negative absorption across the Philadelphia office market. This indicates a localized strength in these specific submarkets, contrasting with the overall slower performance of the city's office sector.
articles.market_intelligence: The broader Philadelphia office market experienced negative absorption in the last quarter.
